key_insight: DynamicVLA combines a compact 0.4B vision-language-action backbone with temporal reasoning and closed-loop adaptation so agents can perceive, anticipate, and continuously control interactions with moving objects in real time.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap where existing VLA models generalize well for static manipulation but fail in dynamic scenarios that require rapid perception, temporal anticipation, and continuous closed-loop control of moving objects.
method: Compact 0.4B VLA architecture with a convolutional vision encoder for spatially efficient, low-latency perception.
Temporal reasoning module that aggregates short-term history to anticipate object motion and inform action planning.
Closed-loop adaptation for continuous control: online feedback from perception updates actions in real time to correct for dynamics and disturbances.
impact: Provides a practical path toward real-time, robust dynamic object manipulation on resource-constrained robots and embodied agents, improving responsiveness and generalization in moving-object tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input (video frames + language), conv-vision encoder, temporal reasoning block, closed-loop controller, and robot actuator.
Temporal timeline or attention map illustrating how past frames influence future action predictions (anticipation visualization).
Closed-loop control loop graphic with perception → policy → action → feedback arrows and latency annotations.
Bar/line chart comparing success rate vs baseline methods and a latency vs model-size tradeoff (highlighting the 0.4B model advantage).
paper_title: DynamicVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
paper_authors: Haozhe Xie, Beichen Wen, Jiarui Zheng, Zhaoxi Chen, Fangzhou Hong
